title: Walmart raises its outlook for the year for the 3rd time after a solid quarter
summary: Walmart reported solid sales for the fiscal quarter as the discounter continues to attract a growing number of customers across the economic spectrum seeking to cut costs in the face of rising prices
story: Walmart reported solid sales for the fiscal quarter as the discounter continues to attract a growing number of customers across the economic spectrum seeking to cut costs in the face of rising prices

NEW YORK -- Walmart reported solid third quarter sales gains as the retailer continues to attract a growing number of customers across the economic spectrum that are seeking to cut costs in the face of rising prices.

The company topped Wall Street’s profit and sales projections, and it raised its annual guidance for the third time this year, but the outlook released Thursday was more conservative than industry analysts had expected.

Comparable sales, which include digital channels and stores, rose 2.9%. That is better than last quarter's 2.6% increase, when Walmart reported its weakest comparable sales growth in six years. But it's still a slowdown from the 4.5% growth registered during the same period last year.

Still, slowing comparable sales, particularly in Walmart stores, also reflect a strategic shift toward e-commerce, Walmart+ memberships and advertising. Global e-commerce sales rose 17%, while U.S. e-commerce sales increased 23% during the latest quarter, the company said.

Walmart said that more than 80% of U.S. e-commerce orders are being fulfilled from stores, including its third party marketplace orders. Stores enabled faster delivery speeds on a wide range of assortments, the retailer said.
Shares rose nearly 1% before the opening bell Thursday.

“We delivered strong results, growing our core business and gaining market share,” Walmart's CEO John Furner said in prepared remarks. “The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more.”

Walmart is considered a barometer of consumer spending given its vast customer base. More than 150 million customers use its website or visit its stores every week, according to Walmart. Analysts look to the massive retailer for clues about what to expect from the industry as a whole during the critical holiday shopping season.

Consumers in the U.S. have remained resilient in the face of painful inflation, but they have also grown more selective about what they buy. Many rely on retailers like Walmart as a one-stop shop for low-priced household goods, groceries and pharmaceuticals.

The latest U.S. retail sales data revealed that shoppers increased spending more slowly in October as Americans pulled back on a variety of purchases, from cars, clothing and furniture and even their own hobbies.
Retail sales rose 0.2% in October, down from a 0.8% gain in September, according to Commerce Department data released this week.
Walmart has been hammering its low price message while refining its store label fashion brands like Scoop and Free Assembly.

Walmart is also trying to increase subscriptions to its shipping programs. During the third quarter, Walmart launched a combined Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus annual membership bundle for $120 per year. The package saves shoppers nearly $100 compared to buying both plans separately, it said.

Walmart, based in Bentonville, Arkansas, has begun to capture a larger share of wealthier consumers. The biggest gains in market share for Walmart have been coming from households with annual incomes over $100,000, the retailer has said.

Walmart’s quarterly net income was $4.94 billion, or 62 cents per share, in the three-month period ended Oct. 31. Adjusted per-share results were 65 cents, higher than the 64 cents Wall Street had expected, according to FactSet. In the year-ago quarter, the company earned $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share.
Sales rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion in the latest quarter. Analysts were predicting $187.38 billion, according to FactSet.

The company said that comparable sales were driven by groceries and general merchandise categories like furniture and toys. But the figure was once again hit by federal legislation that requires pharmacies to dispense some high-cost Medicare drugs at capped prices, the retailer said.

For the full year, Walmart now projects earnings per share to be in the range of $2.84 to $2.89, up from the prior guidance of $2.80 to $2.87. Sales should be up anywhere from 4.9% to 5.2%, up from the prior forecast of 4% to 5%. That would mean a forecast for sales in the range of $748.12 billion to $750.25 billion, according to FactSet.
Analysts expected $2.89 per share and sales of $752.68 billion for the year, according to FactSet.

title: Japan's PM Takaichi says Russia and Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says that she met with Russian President Vladimir Putin for more than 30 minutes in the first such encounter between the two countries’ leaders in seven years
story: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says that she met with Russian President Vladimir Putin for more than 30 minutes in the first such encounter between the two countries’ leaders in seven years

SHENZHEN, China -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Thursday that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks and agreed to keep communicating in the first such encounter between the two countries’ leaders in seven years.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, she said she raised the issue of Moscow’s treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia and urged Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for alleged spying during their meeting late Wednesday in Shenzhen, China.
“We reached an agreement to maintain communication at various levels, including direct contact between the president and myself,” Takaichi said.
Japan's ties with Russia have long been strained by a territorial dispute dating back decades.

Japan lodged a protest with Russia in October over the arrest of a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on suspicion of spying, demanding that Moscow provide an explanation, consular access and humane treatment.

Moscow recently seized control of some local subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco, the largest cigarette maker in Russia, and the company reported it expects a 724 billion yen ($4.5 billion) loss for this year due to the takeover.

Earlier, Japan Tobacco had forecast a 662 billion yen profit for the financial year ending Dec. 31. The company said it has not given up legal ownership of the Russia-based subsidiaries or withdrawn from operating in Russia.

Tensions rose in August after Putin visited Iturup, one of four Russian-controlled islands off Japan’s northern coast that Tokyo also claims. Earlier this month, Tokyo protested after two Russian aircraft briefly violated Japanese airspace off southwestern Japan.

The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Putin is attending the annual APEC summit for the first time in nine years. He, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a summit meeting Thursday after the APEC gathering, an event that seems to underscore Japan's diminished role as a global power.
Takaichi herself was given a very minimal reception on her arrival in Shenzhen, provoking speculation over a deliberate snub by her hosts.
When asked, Takaichi said she did not believe the summit between Xi, Trump and Putin would undermine Japan’s interests.

“We have been maintaining close communication with the United States and other allies while carefully monitoring the impact on the international situation and we will continue to respond appropriately,” Takaichi said. "We do not believe that Japan’s interests will be compromised.”
She did not elaborate on efforts to repair damage to Japan’s ties with China following remarks she made nearly a year ago about Taiwan.
“China is an important neighbor. Given the various issues and challenges that exist between Japan and China, I believe it is essential to engage in dialogue and maintain communication," she said.
Yamaguchi reported from Tokyo. Associated Press journalist Haruka Nuga in Tokyo contributed to this report.

title: Wall Street tumbles to its longest losing streak since 2024 as the Dow drops 1,100 points
summary: The U.S. stock market tumbled again as AI stocks kept falling on worries their boom may be over
story: The U.S. stock market tumbled again as AI stocks kept falling on worries their boom may be over

NEW YORK -- The U.S. stock market tumbled again as beaten-down stocks tied to artificial intelligence kept falling Thursday on worries their breathtaking boom may be over. The losses came even though a leading AI lab, Anthropic, found a strong welcome for the debut of its own stock on Wall Street.

The S&P 500 dropped 2% for a sixth straight loss. That’s its longest losing streak in two and a half years, and the index at the heart of many 401(k) accounts is now down 8.2% from its all-time high set last month.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101 points, or 2.2%, while the Nasdaq composite sank 2.3%.
The losses were widespread, and more than 90% of the stocks that make up the S&P 500 index fell.

Leading them downward was Williams-Sonoma, which dropped 15.2% after the company behind Pottery Barn and West Elm reported revenue for the latest quarter that was a bit weaker than Wall Street expected. It also stuck with its forecast for how much revenue it will make throughout 2026, and the midpoint of that range was below what analysts were expecting.
Walmart sank 1% even though it reported profit and revenue for the latest quarter that edged past analysts’ expectations.
For a while Thursday morning, gains for several AI-related stocks seemed to be enough to more than make up for such losses.

The S&P 500 jumped as much as 1.3% after Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, sold shares of its stock at $83 apiece in its initial public offering. That’s more than the $70 to $78 it earlier thought it would get, and its price quickly surged above $115 after it began trading on the Nasdaq shortly before noon.
Anthropic later pared its gain and finished the day at $97.17, still up 17.1%.

Even before its stock began trading, the strong demand for Anthropic’s IPO appeared to demonstrate faith remained among investors in the AI revolution. The industry needed a boost following sharp recent drops for AI-related stocks on worries their prices shot too high in the frenzy around the technology.
But AI stocks quickly returned to their jittery ways in what Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, called “a very turbulent, white-knuckle period.”
Micron Technology, whose sales of memory for computers have soared because of the AI boom, initially rallied 7.8% and then swung to a loss of 2.1%.
CoreWeave, a company that buys AI chips and rents out access to them to customers over the cloud, went from a 10.5% leap in the morning to a drop of 6.1%.
Nvidia erased its early gain of 4.7% and flipped to a loss of 3.3% amid the lengthening list of worries dogging the entire industry.

At first it was criticism that AI stocks had broadly gone into a bubble after shooting so high, along with doubts that AI could produce enough profit and productivity to make the massive investments in data centers worth it. Then it was worries that high interest rates would mean less borrowed money to fund the industry’s growth. Then came this month’s sweeping victories for Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections, which raised concerns about more regulation for AI.

Most recently, it was the sudden resignation of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO. He was one of AI’s biggest evangelists and helped build interest in the industry while using some of Nvidia’s massive profits to further fund its growth.
Other companies, meanwhile, offered more encouraging signals about AI.

Palo Alto Networks climbed 6.4% after the AI cybersecurity company topped analysts’ expectations for profit and revenue in the latest quarter. It also agreed to buy Applied Compute, a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight AI models, to help customers adopt AI securely. The all-stock deal is valued at $4.5 billion.

Everpure, a company that helps businesses manage and store their data, said its revenue jumped last quarter by more than analysts expected in part because of AI-related offerings. Everpure’s stock rose 4.7%.
All told, the S&P 500 fell 147.80 points to 7,175.83. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 to 49,097.06, and the Nasdaq composite sank 550.69 to 23,879.20.

In the bond market, Treasury yields eased as the drops for stock prices sent investors toward investments seen as safer. When prices for Treasury bonds go up, their yields go down, and the yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 5.04% from 5.07% Wednesday.

Also weighing on yields were a couple reports on the U.S. economy that came in weaker than economists expected. One said slightly more U.S. workers applied for unemployment benefits last week, though the number remains low compared with history. Another said manufacturing growth in the mid-Atlantic region is slowing by more than economists expected.

In stock markets abroad, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.7%. Helping to lead the way was SoftBank Group, which climbed 4.6%. It was an early investor in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and competitor to Anthropic.
South Korea’s Kospi climbed 1.4% thanks to strength for its stocks tied to the AI boom, but stocks were weaker elsewhere in Asia and in Europe. Germany’s DAX lost 1.1%.
AP Business Writer Chan Ho-him contributed to this report.

title: Skydance to combine Warner Bros. TV Group and Paramount Television Studios
summary: Skydance is combining Warner Bros
story: Skydance is combining Warner Bros

NEW YORK -- NEW YORK (AP) — Skydance will combine two of its key TV production units, Warner Bros. Television Group and Paramount Television Studios, bringing such shows as "The Pitt,” “Ted Lasso,” “Reacher” and “Landman” under the same roof.

The combined entity will be known as Warner Bros. Television Studios, with Channing Dungey and Matt Thunell serving as presidents. The merger of the studios will be completed in early 2027, according to a memo released Wednesday.

“Bringing together two of the industry’s most prolific television studios creates a formidable creative engine, uniting extraordinary talent, resources, acclaimed programming and iconic franchises with the global scale to compete at the highest level," George Cheeks, co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance TV, said in the memo.
It’s the latest move since Skydance-owned Paramount last month closed its $81 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, ushering in a new Hollywood giant under the leadership of David Ellison.
The new Warner Bros. Television Studios will house more than 120 TV series, including HBO's “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone,” Netflix's “Emily in Paris” and CBS' “Marshals.”
CBS Studios — another studio that produces shows such as the “NCIS” and “Fire Country” franchises — will continue to operate as a standalone entity under David Stapf.

title: Why France is sending soldiers into Ukraine and how Russia is responding
summary: Russia is responding forcefully to France's confirmation that it periodically sends military personnel into Ukraine for training and maintenance help with supplied weaponry
story: Russia is responding forcefully to France's confirmation that it periodically sends military personnel into Ukraine for training and maintenance help with supplied weaponry

PARIS -- Russia is responding forcefully to confirmation from France that it periodically sends military personnel into Ukraine to provide training and maintenance help with some of the weaponry it has supplied for the war.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said: “This is no longer ‘support for Ukraine,' but direct participation in the war.”
France says the soldiers and weapons specialists are noncombatants.
“Since we are not at war with Russia, these, in fact, are not combat units,” French Deputy Defense Minister Alice Rufo said.
Here's a closer look:
Speaking on Wednesday to French broadcaster RMC, Rufo said French personnel are “a very long way from the front line. They come to carry out occasional missions.”

She didn't specify their numbers, but said that they are “a few soldiers, specialists, including armaments engineers, who work — or can come to work — on an occasional basis to maintain complex equipment, such as Mirage aircraft or Caesar howitzers, and provide targeted training on certain equipment.”

France first delivered Mirage 2000-5 fighters last year to Ukraine and trained pilots and mechanics for them. The French Defense Ministry says the aircraft have helped fend off missile and drone attacks.
It also says that with donations from allies and purchases, Ukraine's force of high-precision French-made Caesar howitzers has grown to become the largest in the world.
France has also supplied precision bombs, cruise missiles, air defense systems, light tanks and other equipment.

Rufo told French lawmakers on Tuesday that France is “accelerating” its support in light of Russia's air campaign against Ukrainian targets. She spoke of a “complete absence of any intention to engage in combat” and described as “absurd” Lavrov's accusation that France is directly participating in the war.
Only a “very limited" number of French personnel are engaged in “the extremely limited” missions, Rufo said.

Her comments came after French media, including broadcaster RFI and Le Monde newspaper, reported that small contingents of French military officers stay in Ukraine for short rotations as part of the so-called Operation Volia, since at least this summer.

French military personnel have been operating in Ukraine for more than six months and France isn't alone in providing such support, Lavrov said Tuesday at a news conference in Manila, Philippines, where he was attending a summit of Southeast Asian nations.

“We have conveyed our concern through the available channels, warning the relevant countries that this is no longer ‘support for Ukraine,’ but direct participation in the war,” he said, without naming the countries.
“This is just like the assistance with target designation, the provision of satellite data and much else,” he said.

Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said that Moscow will regard any foreign troops in Ukraine as legitimate targets and it will be up to the Russian military to determine a response.

The United Kingdom has soldiers in Ukraine, but officials haven't disclosed how many or what their role is. The U.K. Defense Ministry confirmed two deaths of British soldiers in Ukraine in the past year, in both cases in accidents.

Since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, dozens of countries have trained more than 100,000 Ukrainian soldiers, at locations outside the country — in France, the U.K., the United States, Poland, Germany and elsewhere — including on Patriot missile batteries, F-16 combat jets and other equipment. They have also trained recruits, officers, medics and other specialists for combat.
Jill Lawless in London, Sylvie Corbet and Catherine Gaschka in Paris, and Lorne Cook in Brussels, contributed to this report.

title: How three leaders donated the $20 million Melinda French Gates gave them with no strings attached
summary: Philanthropist Melinda French Gates launched a $240 million Global Leaders program in 2024, through her philanthropic organization Pivotal, where she gave $20 million each to 12 luminaries without warning or requirements other than donating the money b...
story: Philanthropist Melinda French Gates launched a $240 million Global Leaders program in 2024, through her philanthropic organization Pivotal, where she gave $20 million each to 12 luminaries without warning or requirements other than donating the money b...
Dr. Alfiee Breland-Noble says she was shocked when philanthropist Melinda French Gates picked her to receive $20 million to donate however she wanted.

The psychologist, author and founder of The AAKOMA Project, a nonprofit supporting the mental health of young people of color, has long admired French Gates’ work, especially in the diversity of her support initiatives. Breland-Noble just never expected to be the focus of one of those initiatives.

“It really was shock and awe,” she said. “My mom just had a knack and a penchant for finding people that nobody else was helping and she would help them. And so for me, the excitement was I get to honor my mother’s legacy by doing the same thing.”

In 2024, through her philanthropic organization Pivotal, French Gates launched the $240 million Global Leaders program, where she gave $20 million each to 12 luminaries, including Breland-Noble, without warning or requirements other than donating the money by the end of 2026. It was part of her plan to donate $1 billion to support women and girls at a time when nonprofits focusing on their issues receive only about 2% of all U.S. philanthropic funding.

Now, with nearly all the money donated, Pivotal has seen enough to call the trust-based philanthropy initiative a “huge success” and is looking for ways to replicate it and encourage other donors to do the same.

“There are so many great ideas out there that might never cross my path but might cross someone else’s,” French Gates said in a statement to The Associated Press. “That’s one reason I started the Global Leaders program: to partner with experts whose firsthand knowledge could broaden Pivotal’s perspective and deepen our impact.”
According to Pivotal, the average grant the Global Leaders handed out was approximately $240,000, with 91% of the donations going to organizations that had not received funding from Pivotal before.

Haven Ley, Pivotal’s chief strategy officer, said a final report on the Global Leaders program will come next year, but that the organization is already looking for ways to build on it. “We did this not just for the impact," Ley said, “but because it was a model that was intriguing to us.”
French Gates said the different vantage points on the world’s challenges have made Pivotal more responsive and helped the Global Leaders be more impactful.
“For me, this is as much about expanding who gets to make decisions about funding as it is about where funding goes,” she said.
For Breland-Noble, being able to donate to others on a grand scale was a meaningful new experience.

Though she has been working in the mental health field for decades, she is relatively new to running her own nonprofit. Breland-Noble established The AAKOMA Project, which stands for African American Knowledge Optimized for Mindfully Healthy Adolescents, in 1999 as an academic research lab, only turning it into a nonprofit in 2018 so that it could put its research findings into action.

To donate the $20 million that French Gates had given her, Breland-Noble created The MATTIE Fund – short for Mindful Advocacy for Totally Transformative Inclusion and Equity, but also named for, and inspired by, her mother Mattie McLeod Breland.

The MATTIE Fund donated to well-established groups like Asian Mental Health Collective. But Breland-Noble made a point of expanding her donations to groups outside her network, searching Google and LinkedIn to find ideas. She asked her Instagram community for recommendations, as well as audiences at her speaking engagements.

Those searches led to her support of BackSpinz Music Academy in North Carolina, which trains young people to use their creativity, and Daddy Stroller Social Club, which helps new fathers deal with postpartum depression.
Breland-Noble said she was thankful to French Gates for the opportunity to give.
“She saw me and supported me and pulled me out – like a needle in a haystack,” said Breland-Noble. “I then had the ability to do that for somebody else.”

Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern said she is also grateful for the opportunity to make $20 million in donations. And she knows she took the decidedly tougher route by not making large gifts to established organizations.
“I wanted to use this funding to achieve things that otherwise may not have existed were it not for this opportunity,” she said. “That took time.”

She began working with the International Rescue Committee on a program to prevent postpartum hemorrhaging for women in areas affected by war and other humanitarian crises, where 58% of maternal mortality occurs. The resulting Safer Births in Crises Consortium now focuses on preventing the deaths of mothers in South Sudan, Burkina Faso and Papua New Guinea.

What Ardern did not anticipate was that her donations through The Matariki Fund for Women would coincide with funding cuts for international aid. As a former prime minister who previously dispatched such aid, she said she had two distinct reactions to seeing life-saving programs cut.

“One is we’ve just got to get on with it. What do we do? How can we help?” Ardern said. “And then I think about how I can advocate for the restoration. How we can lift the profile of this collective approach to voters? Because ultimately, they’re the ones that demand from their leaders that we keep having this impact.”
Ardern said she has no plans to become a full-time philanthropist. She prefers her new job at the University of Sydney as a professor, announced last month.

“I’ll be working on empathetic leadership, but I’m also attached to the School of Public Health," she said, adding that she intends to continue working on global health issues. “My view is there is absolutely a role for political leadership to rebuild trust, reduce insularity, and reduce the grievance that people feel. Actually, what’s interesting is that the public think that it’s their job too.”
Gary Barker, on the other hand, not only used the $20 million he received from French Gates to expand his philanthropic work, he used it to convince other funders to also support his nonprofit.

Barker is the founder and CEO of the Equimundo Center for Masculinities and Social Justice, which engages men and boys in promoting gender equality, and launched the Caring Masculinity Fund to distribute French Gates’ donation.

“The Minderoo Foundation in Australia looked at what Melinda funded us to do and said, ‘Would you come do the same at the country level in Australia?’,” said Barker. “Her voice saying, ‘This is worth investing in and that this is not taking funds or attention away from women and girls’ is a political boost in addition to boosting our credibility as an organization.”
Barker said the experience has made him seek similar relationships with funders.
“We don’t want to go back to piecemeal fundraising,” he said. “We’re not gonna wanna do it any differently from here on out.”

title: Target will take momentum from strong third quarter into the holiday shopping season
summary: Target is reporting its strong quarterly sales gains in roughly five years, fueled by a revitalized product lineup, expanded same-day deliveries and price cuts that brought in customers battered by inflation
story: Target is reporting its strong quarterly sales gains in roughly five years, fueled by a revitalized product lineup, expanded same-day deliveries and price cuts that brought in customers battered by inflation

NEW YORK -- Target delivered its strong quarterly sales gains in roughly five years, fueled by a revitalized product lineup, expanded same-day deliveries and price cuts that brought in customers battered by inflation.
The company raised its annual earnings and sales outlook again on Wednesday after an encouraging third quarter.

Target reported a better-than-expected 7.1% increase in net sales, the best performance since the fourth quarter of 2021. The company also posted its third straight quarter of quarterly comparable sales, which include sales from online and its physical stores.

Sales made through digital channels operating for at least 12 months increased 9.8% from the same quarter last year, while comparable sales at established stores rose 4.6%. The three-month period that ended Oct. 31 overlapped with back-to-school shopping season.
Shares were essentially flat before the opening bell.

The Minneapolis retailer reported growth in a majority of its six core merchandise categories, led by electronics, gaming equipment, sporting goods, toys, trading cards and collectibles, a category Target refers to as "Fun 101.” It also cited higher sales of beauty products, food and beverages.

But Target CEO Michael Fiddelke, a 20-year company veteran who became chief executive in February, told reporters this week that the sales momentum was not limited to certain categories or based on any one initiative. He said Target has seen business pick up across its markets among shoppers of all incomes.
“It’s the cumulative impact of changes across our business that is driving this guest preference for Target,” Fiddelke said.
The company said November net sales so far are in line with the full-year outlook.

Together, comparable store and digital sales in August, September and October increased 5.6% though that figure is being compared to a 2.7% drop in the year-ago period. The retailer also reported a 5.6% gain in the first quarter and a 3.8% uptick in the second quarter of this year.

In March, Fiddelke unveiled a multibillion dollar investment plan aimed at reversing a post-pandemic sales slump. The overhaul included a focus on stocking products and brands that would help restore Target's reputation as a place to go for affordable yet stylish items.

Target launched a new Target Beauty Studio concept in more than 600 locations in September. The new area, which features upscale beauty products and staff trained to offer advice, partly replaced the Ulta shops that were in some stores before Target and Ulta Beauty ended their partnership in August.
Company executives said work to improve the offerings in Target's clothing and home goods departments was ongoing.

With U.S. consumers expressing concerns about the U.S. economy and their own finances, Target also has promoted price reductions this year, including cuts on nearly 2,000 additional items during the third quarter.
The company said most of the new items it has for the holiday shopping season cost $20 or less, including thousands priced at $5 and under.

Target is one of the first big retailers to report third-quarter earnings. The results could give industry analysts and economists another read on how U.S. consumers responded to ongoing inflation pressure before the end-of-year holidays.

Target said it earned $1.21 billion, or $2.65 per share, including a 50-cent benefit from a government tariff refund. In the third quarter of 2025, the company reported $689 million, or $1.51 per share.
Net sales rose 7.1% to $27.07 billion compared to $25.27 billion in the year-ago period.
Analysts were expecting $2.08 per share on net sales of $26.5 billion, according to FactSet.
Target now expects net sales for the full year to be up roughly 6%, one percentage point higher than the guidance it gave in August.
The company projected full-year earnings per share of $10.65 to $11.40. That includes a $2.14 tariff refund benefit. In August, the company expected earnings of $9.90 to $10.90 per share.
Analysts were projecting profits of $10.25 per share on sales of $110.27 billion.

title: After a 13-year wait, 'Grand Theft Auto VI' arrives with enormous hype and expectations
summary: The global rollout of "Grand Theft Auto VI" is underway, taking players back to Vice City
story: The global rollout of "Grand Theft Auto VI" is underway, taking players back to Vice City
LOS ANGELES -- After a 13-year wait, “Grand Theft Auto VI” has begun its global rollout, sending players back to Vice City and kicking off one of the most anticipated entertainment launches in years.
Players in New Zealand were among the first to enter Rockstar Games’ sprawling Florida-inspired world as midnight Thursday arrived, hours before the game becomes available across the United States.

Internet providers there had prepared for a massive surge in downloads. Chorus New Zealand expected about 35 petabytes — 35 million gigabytes — of additional traffic across its network as players downloaded the massive game.

“The game file size at 212 gigabytes is unprecedented,” said Kurt Rodgers, the company’s network strategy manager. “That’s more than a quarter of the average household’s data usage in an entire month, all in one go.”
In Wellington, Adam Simmons launched the game from his living room as soon as it unlocked, keeping the volume low so he wouldn’t wake his wife and daughters.
“The gameplay dynamics are just amazing and the graphics are great and you can tell that the storytelling is really deep,” he said after about half an hour of play.
Shares of Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent company, rose more than 8% Wednesday as the rollout continued.

In the Dallas area, Bryan Banuelos, a mobile auto detailer, told customers he wouldn't be taking calls Thursday so he could focus on “GTA VI.” His social media post actually drove some business beforehand, with customers trying to get their cars detailed before he disappeared into Vice City.
“Tomorrow will be the beginning of a new era for the gamers that like GTA,” Banuelos said.

The “Grand Theft Auto” franchise has sold more than 470 million units worldwide. “Grand Theft Auto V,” released in 2013, accounts for more than 230 million of those sales and generated $1 billion in retail sales in just three days.

Rockstar returns to Vice City, its fictionalized version of Miami, with two new protagonists, a sprawling Florida-inspired world and the pressure of following one of the most successful entertainment products ever released.

At the center of “GTA VI” are Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a couple whose attempts to improve their lives pull them deeper into the criminal underworld of Leonida, Rockstar’s fictionalized version of Florida.

Lucia has recently been released from prison, while Jason is a former soldier who became involved with drug runners in the Leonida Keys. When a criminal job goes wrong, the pair become entangled in a wider conspiracy.
The focus on their relationship marks a major departure from “Grand Theft Auto V,” which followed three playable protagonists.

Rockstar has promoted Leonida as its largest and most detailed open world yet, extending beyond Vice City to beaches, highways, wetlands, nightlife districts and smaller communities inspired by South Florida.

Developers immersed themselves in the region while building the game, driving through Miami, the Florida Keys and surrounding communities, flying over the Everglades and researching the area’s history and architecture.

Miami and surrounding communities have leaned into their connection to Vice City ahead of the release, with businesses, sports teams and local governments using the game’s arrival as a marketing opportunity.

Miami-Dade County entered into a $3.9 million promotional deal with Rockstar that includes a giant “Welcome to Vice City” display atop the Miami Heat’s Kaseya Center. The NBA team is also scheduled to wear black-and-pink Vice City uniforms on the eve of the game’s release.

The campaign has not been universally welcomed. Some South Florida officials have questioned whether public resources should be used to promote a franchise known for car theft, gunplay and other criminal activity.
Supporters have argued that the enormous attention surrounding “GTA VI” gives the region an opportunity to capitalize on a global spotlight.
In Seoul, a giant advertisement draped the side of a building, while Warner Music will host a party at a bar Thursday themed around the game’s soundtrack.
Few entertainment releases arrive with this much anticipation.

The first “GTA VI” trailer drew more than 93 million YouTube views in its first 24 hours, while Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent company, has said the second trailer generated more than 475 million views across platforms in a day.
The game also has attracted awards attention before most players have had a chance to explore it.

“GTA VI” received eight nominations Tuesday for the Game Awards, including game of the year, game direction, narrative, art direction, score and music, audio design, action/adventure and performance. The awards will be presented Dec. 10.

The long wait is partly a product of the extraordinary staying power of its predecessor. “Grand Theft Auto Online,” the multiplayer component of “GTA V,” has kept players engaged for years through updates, activities and in-game purchases.
Music has long been woven into the “Grand Theft Auto” experience, with fictional radio stations and carefully curated soundtracks accompanying players as they drive through the series’ cities.
“Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album,” a 34-track collection of original songs tied to the game, is scheduled for release Friday.

A separate 30-track “Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score” by Grammy-winning French electronic duo Justice is scheduled for release Dec. 11. The adaptive score is designed to shift depending on where players are and what they are doing and includes collaborations involving Tame Impala, SZA, King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard and Gesaffelstein.
Despite years of trailers and promotional material, Rockstar has kept significant portions of “GTA VI” under wraps.

The full voice cast has not been revealed, including the performers behind Lucia and Jason. Actor Stephen Root has confirmed to The Associated Press that he appears in the game, though Rockstar has not publicly identified his role.
Questions also remain about the full range of characters, locations, activities and gameplay systems waiting inside Leonida.
Associated Press journalists Charlotte Graham-McLay in Wellington, New Zealand, and Tong-hyung Kim in Seoul contributed to this report.

title: US futures point higher led by rebound for Nvidia
summary: Tech stocks are leading U.S. futures higher after Nvidia easily exceeded Wall Street expectations as it deals with the abrupt departure of CEO Jensen Huang
story: Tech stocks are leading U.S. futures higher after Nvidia easily exceeded Wall Street expectations as it deals with the abrupt departure of CEO Jensen Huang
HONG KONG -- Tech stocks are leading U.S. futures higher Wednesday after Nvidia easily exceeded Wall Street expectations as it deals with the abrupt departure of CEO Jensen Huang.
Futures for the S&P 500 rose 0.6%, while those for the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.2%. Futures on the tech-heavy Nasdaq advanced 1%.
Oil prices are continuing on a downward trajectory despite new attacks by Iran that threaten to disrupt the shipment of Middle East crude through the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
Prices declined after the American Petroleum Institute said that U.S. crude inventories rose by 5.3% last week, a boost that far exceeded projections from energy analysts.

Chipmakers are surging early after Nvidia reported that its revenue doubled from last year to $116 billion. Nvidia shares are up 4% in premarket trading. Broadcom, Arm Holdings and Advanced Micro Devices are following closely behind.

Retail stocks are mixed after Target raised its outlook for the year following its strongest sales growth in nearly five years. Despite the strong performance, shares dipped 3% and Walmart, which reports quarterly earnings Thursday, fell more than 1%.

President Donald Trump landed in China on Wednesday with trade likely to be the focus of talks with China's leader, Xi Jinping, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left the administration scrambling to calm the American public.
Later on Wednesday, the U.S. Federal Reserve will release minutes from its most recent meeting, with new indications that it has yet to tame inflation.

The persistence of elevated inflation makes it highly likely that the Fed will raise benchmark interest rates at its next meeting in December. It kept rates unchanged late last month, after raising them in September. The Fed increases borrowing costs in an effort to cool spending and bring down inflation.
The 10-year Treasury yield climbed toward 5.15% early Wednesday.
In midday European trading, Germany’s DAX slipped 0.1% to 26,045.57, while France’s CAC 40 edged 0.1% lower to 8,210.70. Britain’s FTSE 100 fell 0.6% to 10,621.79.

U.K. inflation in October rose to 3.6%, the highest level in a year, according to the Office for National Statistics on Wednesday. Rising fuel costs drove much of the increase, adding pressure on the Bank of England to raise the interest rate.
In Asia, the Kospi in Seoul closed 2% higher at 5,067.44 as memory chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 4.2% and Samsung Electronics gained 2.3%.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng fell 0.9% to 23,294.75, while the Shanghai Composite index edged 0.1% lower to 3,587.83.
The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil is down slightly to $93.10. U.S. benchmark crude oil dropped less than a percent to $85.50 per barrel.
The U.S. dollar edged up to 159.38 Japanese yen from 159.37 yen late Tuesday. The euro fell to $1.0966 from $1.0999.

title: Long-lost Georgia O’Keeffe painting found in Manhattan closet sells for $4.8M
summary: A painting dug out of a New York City closet this year after being stashed away since the 1980s has sold at auction for $4.8 million
story: A painting dug out of a New York City closet this year after being stashed away since the 1980s has sold at auction for $4.8 million
NEW YORK -- A long-lost Georgia O’Keeffe painting that had been buried in the closet of a Manhattan apartment for decades sold at auction Tuesday for $4.8 million.

The 1930 landscape painting “Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I” is likely the first in a series of three works depicting Lobo Peak in northern New Mexico, according to Christie’s auction house. Its existence was known from a 1931 photograph, but its whereabouts had been kept secret until recently.

A Manhattan woman in her 90s nonchalantly told her niece one day in 2022, “Oh, by the way, there’s a Georgia O’Keeffe in the closet.” Her family believes she received the painting as a graduation gift from her mother, who had purchased it in 1963 from a New York gallery for $3,800.

The woman, who died recently, displayed it in her East Village apartment for many years until the mid-’80s when she noticed a guest looking at it a little too closely. From then on she kept it in her closet, safely hidden behind coats and boxes.

When the family finally unboxed it this year, they discovered it has all the hallmarks of O’Keeffe’s work, including her signature marking on the back: a star with her initials scrawled in the middle.

The 10-x-24-inch (25.4-x-61-centimeter) oil painting is among O’Keeffe's early love letters to New Mexico, where she settled and lived for decades. The identity of the winning bidder was not disclosed; it sold for $4,878,000.

Known as the “mother of American modernism,” O’Keeffe maintained a home and studio in Abiquiu and a nearby summer residence tucked between the red-rock cliffs of Ghost Ranch. She died in 1986 at age 98 and is best known for her paintings of flowers and American Southwest landscapes.
The second piece in the “Near Abiquiu, New Mexico” collection is at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art, and the other, for many years, was in the collection of the Rockefeller family.

title: Swenn Larsson cuts through fog to lead Gurgl slalom first run, chasing 1st World Cup win in 2 years
summary: Swedish skier Anna Swenn Larsson leads after the first run of the women’s slalom in Austria
story: Swedish skier Anna Swenn Larsson leads after the first run of the women’s slalom in Austria
GURGL, Austria -- Swedish skier Anna Swenn Larsson was targeting her first World Cup win in more than two years as she led after the first run of the women’s slalom on Saturday.

Swenn Larsson was fastest through the fog down the Kirchenkar course in Gurgl, Austria. She finished 0.24 seconds ahead of Lara Colturi and 0.26 ahead of Lara Della Mea as a number of later starters had surprising runs as the fog lifted.

The 35-year-old Swenn Larsson, who claimed bronze in the slalom at the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics earlier this year, has only won twice on the World Cup circuit — with the last of those victories coming in February, 2024.

The women’s slalom season will be marked by the reduced presence of Mikaela Shiffrin in a discipline that she has dominated. The Olympic slalom champion is reducing the number of starts in her strongest discipline and putting more focus on giant slalom and super-G. She is calling this campaign an “exploration season.”
Several later starters were among the leading 10 in Gurgl, including American skier AJ Hurt, who was sixth fastest, 0.55 behind Swenn Larsson.
Paula Moltzan was 11th fastest, 1.16 off the pace. The American secured her first career World Cup win last month when the women’s Alpine ski racing season opened with a giant slalom.
Colturi was second in that race as well as in last week’s slalom in Levi, Finland. That was won by Emma Aicher, who was 13th after Saturday’s opening run.

title: Australia wins the toss and will bowl in the 1st of 5 T20 matches against England
summary: Australia has won the toss and decided to bowl in the first of five Twenty20 cricket internationals at the Melbourne Cricket Ground
story: Australia has won the toss and decided to bowl in the first of five Twenty20 cricket internationals at the Melbourne Cricket Ground
MELBOURNE, Australia -- Australia won the toss and decided to bowl in the first of five Twenty20 cricket internationals on Saturday at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Henry Crocombe will make his T20 debut for England after making his ODI debut earlier this year.
England won the one-day international series 2-1, including a 97-run win in the decider at Hobart on Wednesday.
The teams play the second T20 on Tuesday at Carrara on the Gold Coast south of Brisbane.

title: JuJu Watkins loses her voice, then finds a 36-point, six-steal game for No. 4 USC in win over Baylor
summary: JuJu Watkins delivered her best performance of the young season for No. 4 Southern California, scoring 36 points in a 78-69 win over Baylor
story: JuJu Watkins delivered her best performance of the young season for No. 4 Southern California, scoring 36 points in a 78-69 win over Baylor
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — JuJu Watkins lost her voice and then found her best performance of the young season for No. 4 Southern California.
She had a season-high 36 points, 11 rebounds and a career-best six steals in the Trojans' 78-69 win over Baylor on Friday night while playing with a cold that turned her voice into a squeak.
“I’m feeling a little better,” she said. “It’s one of the best feelings to be out here.”
Watkins got the biggest cheers of any player from the crowd of 3,390 at Intuit Dome, the NBA arena located about seven miles west of the Watts neighborhood where she grew up.
“I never really thought I would be here playing,” she said. “During the game, I looked up and was like, ‘Wow, we’re really playing Intuit Dome.' Hopefully, we get more women's games in here.”

Watkins notched her 23rd career game with at least 30 points, leaving her two shy of tying Hall of Famer Cheryl Miller’s school record of 25 and USC improved to 22-1 when Watkins scores at least 30 points.
“JuJu got us,” Baylor coach Nicki Collen said.
Watkins is trying to get her feel back after missing all of last season while rehabbing from ACL surgery.
“I've been for so long so honestly I’m taking every game and trying to learn as much as possible and translate it to the next game,” she said.

Coming off a loss to then-No. 1 South Carolina, the Trojans (4-1) got pummeled in the first quarter. Baylor scored the first eight points before Watkins hit a 3-pointer coming out of a timeout. USC fell behind by 15 points and trailed 26-15 after Taliah Scott scored 15 of her 24 points in the opening quarter.
Watkins' pair of free throws put USC ahead 41-40 at halftime. Then she took over.
She hit a 3-pointer to open the third and closed it grabbing her own offensive rebound and scoring for a 64-57 lead. She ran off eight straight points in the fourth.
“The ball would end up back in JuJu's hands late in the shot clock and she would start boogieing,” Collen said. “She got in that mode where she wanted to prove she was the best player in the gym.”
The teams met for the first time since USC beat the Bears 74-70 in the 2024 NCAA Tournament Sweet 16 when Watkins had 30 points, six rebounds, four assists and four blocks as a freshman.

“There's a totally different effort on the defensive end,” Cullen said, comparing Watkins then and now. “She's made a huge jump in that area. I think she has a chance to be a really elite two-way player at the next level."

Five games into the season, Watkins is already getting asked about her future plans. She could declare for the WNBA draft next spring or stay for a final season under the NCAA's eligibility rules that allow athletes five years to complete their careers.
“I really can’t really say what I’m doing because I don’t know,” she said. “I’m just locked in on everything we have going on here.”

title: Mantas Juzenas scores 25, Saint Mary’s defeats Saint Louis 95-78
summary: Mantas Juzenas had 25 points and 10 rebounds to help Saint Mary’s beat Saint Louis 95-78
story: Mantas Juzenas had 25 points and 10 rebounds to help Saint Mary’s beat Saint Louis 95-78
MORAGA, Calif. -- Mantas Juzenas had 25 points and 10 rebounds to help Saint Mary’s beat Saint Louis 95-78 on Friday.

Evangelos Zougris added 23 points and seven rebounds while shooting 9 of 14 from the field and 5 for 5 from the free-throw line for the Gaels (5-1). Jeremy Dent-Smith shot 3 of 10 from the field, including 1 for 6 from 3-point range, and went 9 for 10 from the foul line to finish with 16 points.

Amari McCottry led the way for the Billikens (3-2) with 21 points and four steals. Saint Louis also got 19 points, eight rebounds and two steals from Kellen Thames. Trey Green finished with 15 points.

Saint Mary’s took the lead for good with 4:56 left in the first half. The score was 42-37 at halftime, with Dent-Smith racking up 10 points. Juzenas scored 19 points in the second half to help lead the way as Saint Mary’s went on to secure a victory, outscoring Saint Louis by 12 points in the second half.

title: David Mager scores 27 as Pepperdine takes down West Coast Baptist 140-54
summary: David Mager led Pepperdine past West Coast Baptist with 27 points off of the bench and Anto Balian scored 22 in a 140-54 victory
story: David Mager led Pepperdine past West Coast Baptist with 27 points off of the bench and Anto Balian scored 22 in a 140-54 victory
MALIBU, Calif. -- David Mager led Pepperdine past West Coast Baptist on Friday with 27 points off of the bench and Anto Balian added 11 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds in a 140-54 victory.

Mager added seven rebounds for the Waves (3-3) and Balian made 7 of 8 from the floor, including 4 for 5 from 3-point range, and 4 for 4 from the free-throw line. Alex Constanza had 20 points and went 8 of 9 from the field (4 for 5 from 3-point range).

Isaias Salgado led the way for the with 12 points. West Coast Baptist, a member of the National Christian College Athletic Association (NCCAA) also got 12 points from Cayden Penha. Jacob Winkelman also had eight points.

Pepperdine took the lead 29 seconds into the game and did not trail again. Constanza led the Waves with 20 points in the first half to help put them up 70-20 at the break. Pepperdine pulled away with a 12-0 run in the second half to extend a 52-point lead to 64 points. The Waves outscored West Coast Baptist by 36 points in the final half, as Mager led the way with a team-high 18 second-half points.

title: No. 16 Washington women beat Stanford 105-50, the Cardinal's worst loss in program history
summary: Brynn McGaughy scored a career-high 21 points, Avery Howell added 20 points on 7-of-10 shooting and No. 16 Washington handed Stanford its worst loss in program history, beating the Cardinal 105-50
story: Brynn McGaughy scored a career-high 21 points, Avery Howell added 20 points on 7-of-10 shooting and No. 16 Washington handed Stanford its worst loss in program history, beating the Cardinal 105-50

SEATTLE -- Brynn McGaughy scored a career-high 21 points, Avery Howell added 20 points on 7-of-10 shooting and No. 16 Washington handed Stanford its worst loss in program history, beating the Cardinal 105-50 on Friday night.
Stanford's previous mark for largest margin of defeat was 49, set Feb. 6, 2025, in a 96-47 loss at then-No. 3 Notre Dame.

Hailee Swain had 12 points on 5-of-15 shooting for Stanford (4-2), which lost for the first time since a 15-point loss to Arizona as part of the Hall of Fame Series at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas to open the season.
Devin Coppinger had 17 points, Saniya Sellers added 12 points, nine assists and three steals and Amayah Garcia scored 10 for Washington (5-0).

Coppinger opened the scoring with a jumper and then hit a 3 before Tilda Trygger converted a three-point play as the Huskies had eight of the first 10 points. McGaughy's layup plus the and-1 free throw capped a 12-0 spurt that made it 20-4 with 1:53 left in the first quarter and Washington scored the first 11 points in a 20-4 run that pushed the lead as high as 31 before halftime.

The Huskies made 17 3s and had more points from behind the arc (51) than Stanford scored in total. They made 38 of 67 (57%) from the field, shot 49% from 3-point range and scored 31 points off 19 Cardinal turnovers.
Washington had its highest-scoring game since a 113-39 win over North Carolina Central on Nov. 9, 2023.
Stanford: Plays Sunday at Portland.
Washington: Hosts Cal Poly on Sunday.

title: Richter throws TD pass to Dabbs, Griffith kicks 4 FGs for Toledo in 19-0 win over BGSU
summary: John Alan Richter threw a 35-yard touchdown pass to Adjatay Dabbs, senior Reice Griffith kicked a career-high four field goals and Toledo beat Bowling Green 19-0 for the Rockets’ fifth consecutive win
story: John Alan Richter threw a 35-yard touchdown pass to Adjatay Dabbs, senior Reice Griffith kicked a career-high four field goals and Toledo beat Bowling Green 19-0 for the Rockets’ fifth consecutive win

TOLEDO, Ohio -- John Alan Richter threw a 35-yard touchdown pass to Adjatay Dabbs, senior Reice Griffith kicked a career-high four field goals and Toledo beat Bowling Green 19-0 on Friday night for the Rockets' fifth consecutive win.

Toledo (9-2) is tied with Western Michigan, Buffalo and Ohio — which the Rockets play in the regular-season finale — atop the Mid-American Conference at 6-1. The top two play the MAC Championship game Dec. 5 in Detroit.

Bowling Green (3-8, 3-4) was 1 of 12 on third-down conversions, 0 for 2 on fourth down and went three-and-out four times. The Falcons had one first down in the first quarter, three in the first half and finished with nine. The
Griffith was good from 46, 29, 39 and 42 yards. He missed a 43-yard attempt a little more than 4 minutes into the game.

Bryson Hammer returned a short punt 12 yards to the Falcons 35. After an incompletion on first down, Richter pumped once and then threw and arcing pass to Dabbs who made a contested catch in the front of the end zone to give Toledo a 16-0 lead with 46 seconds left in the first half.

The Falcons put together an eight-play, 51-yard drive (their longest by either count) in the second quarter, aided by Nakai Amachree's 20-yard run on the first play and Austin Novosad third-and-3 pass deep down the middle to Joseph Saffold for 21 yards. BGSU's only trip beyond the Toledo 34-yard line ended at the 14 with a missed 32-yard attempt byTravis Kenner that bounced off the left upright.
Bowling Green: Hosts UMass in the regular-season finale on Nov. 28.
Toledo: Visits Ohio next Friday.

title: No. 4 USC rallies from 15 down behind JuJu Watkins to beat Baylor 78-69 at Intuit Dome
summary: JuJu Watkins scored a season-high 36 points to lead No. 4 Southern California to a 78-69 comeback win over Baylor
story: JuJu Watkins scored a season-high 36 points to lead No. 4 Southern California to a 78-69 comeback win over Baylor

INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- JuJu Watkins scored a season-high 36 points and No. 4 Southern California rallied from an early 15-point deficit to beat Baylor 78-69 on Friday night at the Hollywood Hardwood Classic in the first women's college basketball game played at Intuit Dome.
Watkins had 11 rebounds and notched her 23rd career game with at least 30 points, leaving her two shy of tying Hall of Famer Cheryl Miller’s school record of 25.
Saniyah Hall added 12 points and seven rebounds despite foul trouble for the Trojans (4-1).

Taliah Scott scored 24 points and made all of her 10 of her free throws, keeping the nation's free-throw shooting leader perfect for the season. Baylor (5-1) traveled 1,200 miles to play its first road game of season at the NBA arena that opened in August 2024.
Scott had 15 points, including her team's first 11, as the Bears raced to a 26-15 lead in the first quarter. The Trojans missed seven of their first nine field goals.

USC clamped down defensively in the second quarter, holding Scott to two points and forcing her into three turnovers. The Trojans took their first lead of the game on Jazzy Davidson's layup after Watkins fired a pinpoint pass from the left side. They led 41-40 at halftime after Watkins hit two free throws.
Baylor tied the game early in the third but Watkins took control. She missed and then scored off her own offensive rebound to end the period ahead 64-57.
The Trojans lead the all-time series 3-1.
The first men's college game played at Intuit Dome was in December 2024, when UCLA defeated Gonzaga.
Baylor: Hosts Northern Kentucky on Sunday.
USC: Hosts Northern Arizona on Monday.

title: Nikola Jokic's big 2nd half sends the Nuggets to a 133-124 win over the Rockets
summary: Nikola Jokic had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds as the Denver Nuggets defeated the Houston Rockets 133-124 in a back-and-forth NBA Cup game
story: Nikola Jokic had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds as the Denver Nuggets defeated the Houston Rockets 133-124 in a back-and-forth NBA Cup game
DENVER -- Nikola Jokic had 26 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds as the Denver Nuggets defeated the Houston Rockets 133-124 in a back-and-forth NBA Cup game Friday night.
Christian Braun and Cameron Johnson each scored 19 for the Nuggets in a matchup that featured 32 lead changes and 17 ties. Neither team led by more than five until there was 2:01 remaining.
The win was Denver's sixth in eight games, the past two of which have come against the Rockets and Boston Celtics, who are a combined 23-9.

Aaron Gordon added 18 points for the Nuggets, while DeMar DeRozan scored 15 and Jamal Murray had 14 points and seven assists. Jokic scored 24 points in the second half, including 18 in the third quarter.

Alperen Sengun, who played the first quarter in goggles after sustaining a scratched cornea in a win Wednesday against Indiana, led the way for Houston with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for his second triple-double this season.

Each of the Rockets’ starters finished with at least 16 points, including 25 from Fred VanVleet, who also had nine assists. Their backups, however, provided only 12 points and combined to miss 13 of 17 shots.
After a 20-foot jumper by VanVleet extended Houston’s lead to five with 5:10 left, Denver countered with 10 straight points in 1:55 and finished the game on a 23-9 run.
The Nuggets improved to 2-0 in the group stage of the NBA Cup, while the Rockets dropped to 1-2.
It was the second meeting in 11 days between the teams. Houston won the first one, 110-100, on Nov. 9.
Rockets: Host the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday.
Nuggets: At the Chicago Bulls on Sunday.

title: Reserves Brown, Copeland send Seton Hall past NC State in Baha Mar Championship, 87-81 in OT
summary: Backup Rodney Brown Jr. scored 24 points and fellow reserve Terry Copeland Jr. added 22 points and Seton Hall beat NC State 87-81 in overtime in the Baha Mar Championship game
story: Backup Rodney Brown Jr. scored 24 points and fellow reserve Terry Copeland Jr. added 22 points and Seton Hall beat NC State 87-81 in overtime in the Baha Mar Championship game

NASSAU, Bahamas -- Backup Rodney Brown Jr. scored 24 points and fellow reserve Terry Copeland Jr. added 22 points and Seton Hall beat NC State 87-81 in overtime in the Baha Mar Championship game on Friday night.
Brown finished 7-of-11 shooting including 4 of 6 from 3-point range. Copeland was near perfect shooting 8 of 9 and 6 of 7 from the foul line. Copeland also grabbed a game-high nine rebounds.
Ven-Allen Lubin scored 27 points making all 11 foul shots, Preston Edmead scored 14 points and reserve Christian Hammond 13 for NC State.
Both teams are 5-1.
Copeland made consecutive layups to send the Pirates ahead 79-75 with 2:55 left in overtime and Seton Hall led for the remainder.
Brown made a pair of foul shots with 28 seconds left, and Elijah Fisher made a pair with two seconds left in the extra quarter to clinch the win.
Lubin made two foul shots with seven seconds left at the end of regulation to tie it at 73. Seton Hall's Mihailo Petrovic missed a shot with two seconds left to force the overtime.
Seton Hall led 30-29 at halftime.
NC State: Hosts Norfolk State on Wednesday.
Seton Hall: Hosts New Hampshire on Tuesday.

title: Jason Crowe Jr. and Bryson Tiller score 18 apiece for Missouri in 91-64 win over Le Moyne
summary: Jason Crowe Jr. and Bryson Tiller scored 18 points apiece to lead five Missouri players in double figures and the Tigers beat Le Moyne 91-64 for their fourth consecutive win
story: Jason Crowe Jr. and Bryson Tiller scored 18 points apiece to lead five Missouri players in double figures and the Tigers beat Le Moyne 91-64 for their fourth consecutive win

COLUMBIA, Mo. -- Jason Crowe Jr. and Bryson Tiller scored 18 points apiece to lead five Missouri players in double figures and the Tigers beat Le Moyne 91-64 on Friday night for their fourth consecutive win.
Kennard Davis Jr. had 13 points, Jamier Jones scored 11 and Toni Bryant 10 for Missouri (5-1).
Khalil Williams, Ty Francis and Trevor Rowe scored 11 points apiece for Le Moyne (2-4).
The Tigers shot 57% from the field, 11 of 25 (55%) from 3-point range, scored 26 points off 16 Le Moyne turnovers and outscored the Dolphins 12-3 in second-chance points.

Crowe hit a jumper that gave Missouri the lead for good less than 5 minutes into the game. Crowe, Pierce and Tiller each hit a 3 in an 85-second span to push the lead into double figures and spark a 17-4 run that culminated with back-to-back dunks by Crowe and Jones and made it 31-15 with 8:26 left until halftime.

Tiller hit a jumper and a 3-pointer that ignited a 12-0 to close the first half. Bryant added a layup and, after Cord Stansberry took a steal coast to coast for a two-hand dunk, made a 3 that gave the Tigers an 28-point lead at halftime.

Jones made two free throws before Crowe stole the inbounds pass, calmly took one dribble to the right corner and knocked down a 3 and Davis followed with a steal and a fast-break dunk 19 seconds later that gave Missouri its biggest lead of the game at 63-26 with 15 minutes to go.
Le Moyne: Hosts Division-II Mansfield on Monday.
Missouri: Hosts Evansville on Tuesday.

title: Devin Booker scores 23 points and Suns pull away in final minute for 111-101 win over Jazz
summary: Devin Booker had 23 points and the Phoenix Suns scored the final six of the game to pull away late and beat the Utah Jazz 111-101 in an NBA Cup matchup
story: Devin Booker had 23 points and the Phoenix Suns scored the final six of the game to pull away late and beat the Utah Jazz 111-101 in an NBA Cup matchup
SALT LAKE CITY -- Devin Booker had 23 points and the Phoenix Suns scored the final six of the game to pull away late and beat the Utah Jazz 111-101 in an NBA Cup matchup Friday night.

With the Suns clinging to a four-point lead in the final minute, Booker made a basket and a free throw and Jalen Green added a dunk and another free throw to clinch Phoenix's fifth victory in six games.
Miles Bridges and Dillon Brooks each had 18 points, and Collin Gillespie scored 16 for the Suns (8-7).

After back-to-back wins in Los Angeles over the Clippers and Lakers, the Jazz reverted to the form they displayed in their earlier 12-game losing streak — poor shooting, sloppiness with the ball and weak defense.
Darryn Peterson had 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists to pace Utah (3-14). Jaxson Hayes added 18 points and 14 boards, while Brice Sensabaugh also scored 18.
The Suns led by double digits most of the game before the Jazz pulled to 96-89 on a twisting layup by Hayes with 6:25 left.
Green responded with five straight points, but the Jazz made one last run — a 9-0 surge — that made it 105-101 with 39.5 seconds remaining on Svi Mykhailiuk's 3-pointer.

The Jazz are still missing their starting frontline of Lauri Markkanen (hand), Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee). Without any interior presence to contend with, the Suns applied a full-court press at times and their defensive ball pressure disrupted Utah's offensive sets on the perimeter.
Utah committed 14 turnovers, leading to 19 Phoenix points.
The Suns have won 13 of the last 14 matchups.
Brooks made a 3 to cap a 15-4 run that gave Phoenix a 39-27 lead with 9:30 left in the second quarter.
Suns: Continue their six-game trip Monday at New Orleans.
Jazz: Host the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday.

title: Luka Doncic scores 25, Lakers barely hold off Kings 106-104 on LaVine's miss at the buzzer
summary: The Los Angeles Lakers held off the Sacramento Kings 106-104 for their 10th victory in 11 games
story: The Los Angeles Lakers held off the Sacramento Kings 106-104 for their 10th victory in 11 games

LOS ANGELES -- Luka Doncic had 25 points and eight assists, Quentin Grimes hit a tiebreaking 3-pointer with 57 seconds to play, and the Los Angeles Lakers rallied in the fourth quarter for their 10th win in 11 games, 106-104 over the Sacramento Kings on Friday night.

Walker Kessler scored 15 points and Matisse Thybulle had 14 for the Lakers, who struggled at home against another rebuilding opponent two nights after their nine-game winning streak ended with a loss to the Utah Jazz.
The Lakers hung on for their fifth straight home victory over Sacramento when Zach LaVine missed a long 3-pointer at the buzzer.

De’Andre Hunter scored a season-high 30 points and hit five 3-pointers for the Kings, who dropped to 1-14 on the season — the worst 15-game start in team history — with their eighth straight loss despite taking a lead into the fourth quarter.

Sacramento led by 11 in the third quarter and took a small advantage into the fourth, but the Lakers built a 101-93 lead with 4 1/2 minutes to play. The Kings responded with eight straight points to tie it on Domantas Sabonis' free throws with 2:32 left.

After Grimes made his only 3-pointer of the night, Doncic made a turnover with 23 seconds left. Kessler then bricked two free throws to give the Kings one last chance, but LaVine pulled up and clanged his final shot off the rim.
LaVine scored 19 points. Sabonis had 19 points and 16 rebounds for Sacramento, and Darius Acuff Jr. had 18 points and 12 assists.
The Lakers improved to 2-1 in NBA Cup play. Sacramento is 0-3.
Austin Reaves missed his fourth straight game with a bruised heel. The Lakers’ second-leading scorer has already missed five of their first 17 games due to injury after missing 31 games last season.
Kessler’s first 3-pointer in a Lakers uniform put LA ahead early in the fourth.
Precious Achiuwa sat out for Sacramento with a leg injury.
Kings: Host Boston on Saturday.
Lakers: Host Utah on Monday.

title: Verstappen takes Las Vegas GP pole after Antonelli’s 5-place grid penalty
summary: Max Verstappen has won the Las Vegas Grand Prix two of its three years, but never sat on the pole until now thanks to a penalty handed to Kimi Antonelli before qualifying Friday night
story: Max Verstappen has won the Las Vegas Grand Prix two of its three years, but never sat on the pole until now thanks to a penalty handed to Kimi Antonelli before qualifying Friday night
LAS VEGAS -- Max Verstappen has won the Las Vegas Grand Prix two of its three years but never sat on the pole until now thanks to a penalty handed to Kimi Antonelli before qualifying Friday night.

Antonelli, the 20-year-old who is this year's Formula 1 champion, put together a time of 1:34.684 in the third qualifying session for Saturday night's race. But he will start sixth because of a five-place penalty because his Mercedes team exceeded its allocation of engines for the season.
Verstappen, a four-time F1 championship who had quite a combative practice session earlier Friday, had a time of 1:35.264.

Conditions for the 3.85-mile course (6.2 kilometers) were considerably different from Thursday's two practices, the first in the rain and the second on the wet surface that remained. The track was dry for Friday's practice and qualifying sessions.

That better simulated expected dry conditions for Saturday night's 50-lap race. Drivers also learned more about driving in what is expected to be one of the colder races in F1 history with a forecast temperate of 47 degrees Fahrenheit (8 degree Celsius) at race time.
Verstappen will go for this race's trifecta. George Russell won two years ago, the same night Verstappen clinched his fourth consecutive series title.

Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc — fourth and fifth in the season standings, respectively — surprisingly failed to get out of the second qualifying session. Leclerc cost himself by not properly handling Turn 7 and didn't get to the checkered flag in time for a final lap to make the time necessary to make the top 10 for the last session.
Leclerc will start 11th on Saturday and Hamilton 12th.

title: James Harden’s new role, same old burst: A 51-point night that moved him past Kobe Bryant
summary: James Harden shows he can still dominate on the court
story: James Harden shows he can still dominate on the court

CLEVELAND -- James Harden's game has evolved over the past couple seasons where he is counted on more for getting open shots for teammates than being the prolific scorer he was during his first 12 years in the league.
On Friday night though, the Cleveland Cavaliers guard showed that he can still have games that leave fans and teammates in awe.
Harden scored 51 points and passed Kobe Bryant for third-most, 50-point games in NBA history as the Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game.

“It’s a different role for me. My usage rate isn’t extremely high every game. We have somebody for that. So mine is kind of scoring when I need to, but then distributing the ball,” Harden said. “My number is called and you need to go out there and put the shots up. Ok, I can still do it. I knew I can do it, but it’s just when you don’t do something consistently and then it goes away a little bit or you just don’t know if you got it or not.”

Harden is at 26 50-point games after being tied with Bryant for nearly year. His last big game was nearly a year ago with the Los Angeles Clippers, when he scored 55 against Charlotte on Nov. 22, 2025.
Michael Jordan is second with 31 while Wilt Chamberlain is the runaway leader with 118.

“When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe, shooting guard position, the best to ever do it. So just to be in that conversation, it’s very humbling and it’s definitely special,” Harden said.

The performance by Harden was the type of game the 18-year veteran had during a run with the Houston Rockets, when he was named the NBA MVP during the 2017-18 season, and had three straight seasons where he averaged at least 30 points a game.

Harden played a season-high 40 minutes was 15 of 26 from the field, including 7 of 11 from beyond the arc. He also made all 14 of his free throws and had six rebounds and six assists for the Cavaliers, who have won three of four but only 9-8 after reaching the Eastern Conference finals last season.

“Nights like that are so special. The crowd appreciated that performance. That wasn’t like we’re 10 games above .500 and everything’s peachy. So it was a clutch performance. We needed that tonight,” coach Kenny Atkinson said.
Harden, who turned 37 in August, also became the sixth NBA player age 37 or older to have a 50-point game, joining Bryant, Jordan, LeBron James, Jamal Crawford and Steph Curry.
Harden said he felt like it was going to be a big night from the opening tip. He scored 15 in the first quarter and was up to 24 at halftime.

“That was vintage where really you can’t do anything if you’re the opposing coach. Especially when he’s getting by you like that, when they started taking away a step back and one or two crosses and he’s in the lane, then there’s just no stopping him," Atkinson said. "There’s really nothing you can do. So vintage, very reminiscent of his Houston days.”

Harden had 42 points after three quarters when the Cavaliers were up 103-82. Indiana made a run to get it within six with two minutes remaining when Harden made one final finishing push. A 3-pointer from the top of the key with 57.9 seconds left extended Cleveland's lead to 124-113 before he made a pair of free throws to get over 50 15 seconds later.

“I think what excites me a lot is even being in my 18th year learning how to still be impactful. It’s easy when you’re young, 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by,” he said, “Now it’s like, you’re not as fast. Can you still give by people or how can you get by somebody? That’s the evolution of James Harden and figuring that out. Tonight was a confidence booster that I can do it at a high level still.”
Harden also became the sixth player in Cavs history to have a 50-point game, and the first since Donovan Mitchell’s 71-point outing on Jan. 2, 2023, against Chicago.

“I think I can speak for every hooper, especially when you’re at that level. Sometimes you just need that. Sometimes you need to just remind yourself just because you’re in such a rare era doesn’t mean you’re not human. And I think for him to tell you guys that, I’m glad he said that because that shows the human side that we all see of him,” Mitchell said.

summary: Hudson Ward had 18 points in Idaho’s 84-81 victory against CSU Bakersfield
story: Hudson Ward had 18 points in Idaho’s 84-81 victory against CSU Bakersfield
MOSCOW, Idaho -- Hudson Ward had 18 points in Idaho’s 84-81 victory against CSU Bakersfield on Friday.

Ward also added five rebounds and three steals for the Vandals (3-3). Kristian Gonzalez scored 14 points while going 6 of 9 (1 for 4 from 3-point range). Kase Wynott had 12 points and shot 4 of 7 from the field, including 1 for 3 from 3-point range, and went 3 for 4 from the line.

title: Air Force runs for 429 yards in 52-3 rout of UTEP
summary: Evan Medders threw two touchdown passes, Air Force ran for 429 yards, and the Falcons swamped UTEP 52-3 on Friday night
story: Evan Medders threw two touchdown passes, Air Force ran for 429 yards, and the Falcons swamped UTEP 52-3 on Friday night
AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. -- Evan Medders threw two touchdown passes, Air Force ran for 429 yards, and the Falcons swamped UTEP 52-3 on Friday night.

Three of the Falcons' four completed passes went for touchdowns, two by Medders and one by Maguire Martin. Medders' touchdowns were 77 yards to Jonah Dawson and 31 yards to Adam Hrynciw. Martin's only pass attempt was a connection with Major Quin on a 35-yard score.
Rocco Conti led Air Force with 64 yards rushing and 18 players had rushing attempts for the Falcons (9-2, 5-2 Mountain West).
Air Force had 586 total yards to UTEP's 116. First downs were 27-6 in favor of Air Force.
Jayden Wilson had 12 total tackles for the Miners (1-10, 0-7).
Air Force and UTEP played for the first time since 1995 when both schools were members of the Western Athletic Conference. Air Force leads the overall series, 15-1, including an 8-0 mark at home.
Air Force wraps up the regular season at New Mexico next Friday.
UTEP finishes at Northern Illinois on Nov. 28. ___

title: Able scores 20 points, Fens makes debut and North Carolina beats Marshall 88-72
summary: Matt Able scored 23 points and Terrence Brown added 20 points and North Carolina beat Marshall 88-72
story: Matt Able scored 23 points and Terrence Brown added 20 points and North Carolina beat Marshall 88-72
CHAPEL HILL, N.C. -- Matt Able scored 23 points, Terrence Brown scored 20 and North Carolina beat Marshall 88-72 on Friday night.
Jarin Stevenson scored 13 points, and center Cameron Fens made his North Carolina debut, scoring nine points and grabbing a team-high eight rebounds in 19 minutes.

Fens — a 7-foot South Dakota transfer — had filed a lawsuit Wednesday in a North Carolina court seeking to recover a year cut short by a misdiagnosed foot injury at his previous school. On Thursday, a judge granted a temporary restraining order for Fens, clearing the way for him to play at least through a hearing set for Nov. 30.
Noah Otshudi scored 14 points and reserve Boubacar Djigo scored 11 points for Marshall (2-4).
The Tar Heels (4-1) built a 25-8 lead with 11 1/2 minutes before halftime before Marshall reeled them in and outscored North Carolina 29-17 and drew within 42-37 at halftime.
North Carolina gradually pulled away and took a double-digit lead for good on Isaiah Denis' layup to make it 67-56 with 11:33 to go.
Marshall hosts Prairie View on Wednesday.
North Carolina hosts Monmouth on Monday.
